newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads pressured, junk mired.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads pressured, junk mired.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond supply pressured spreads on Thursday and players reported indigestion ahead of potent economic data on Friday.

A handful of high-yield issues were priced, meanwhile, but reflected no appreciation in market tone. In fact, just as many issues were postponed on Thursday as market fundamentals remained pitted against fresh paper, players said.

While still cautious on the market, Kingman Penniman, president of KDP Investment Advisors Inc, said suddenly attractive secondary levels have begun to take precedence for available investor cash. Corporate treasurers, therefore, might do better by avoiding the competition with secondary bonds altogether, he said.
Of 100 bonds, KDP has increased its buy percentage to 24 percent on Thursday from a record low 7.7 percent one month ago, Penniman said.

But Penniman, buysiders and dealers all agree the marketplace is still in the doldrums and may be in for another dose of selling should widely-watched AMG Data Services report outflows for the third consecutive week.
New deals priced on Thursday were a hard sell, dealers said, with investors demanding significant chunks of additional yield and/or equity to buy.

UroHealth Systems Inc's $110 million seven-year senior subordinated notes, according to a buy-side source, went through several rounds of pricing attempts before getting done with warrants for two to four percent of the company.
A $100 million Bellwether Exploration Corp 10-year issue came at a spread of 400 basis points over Treasuries, behind the bandied about 350 to 375 basis point price talk.
Bear Stearns & Co led the UroHealth deal and J.P. Morgan Securities led the Bellwether deal.
Postponements became more commonplace on Thursday with the shelving of $220 million debt from Bank United Corp, $80 million from Prime Matrix Communications, and $150 million from Station Casinos.

On the buy-side, George Edwards, a portfolio manager with Prudential Investments, said the secondary does present better value in spots, but it's too soon to jump back into the secondary with reckless abandon.

"We are fairly typical of a lot of mutual funds and we just go into our shell in a market like this because it's hard to project what redemptions are going to be," Edwards said. "We don't want to go wild and spend all our cash just because we want to be cautious...we don't do a lot of bottom fishing until it looks like things have firmed and redemptions have quieted down."
Fund outflows of $500 to $750 million for the latest week may well lead to another round of selling, he added.

Reflecting the potential for rapid gains, Trump Castle first mortgage debt has risen about six points in two days to 81 bid thanks to heavy short covering, sources said. Talk of a viable investor to replace the abandoned Colony Resources Inc investment also shored up bids, one source said.

Turning to investment grades, dealers reported indigestion and reluctant buyers for some big new issues on Thursday in the advent of Friday's March employment report. Several bid lists of short paper were reported from managers looking to raise cash that may be put to work after the jobs report, traders said.
"The tone is that there is a lot of buyers on the sidelines," said a trader at a West Coast investment firm.

He added "The 10-year T-note has ticked up for the past few days -- people are starting to buy into this thing and the only reason it's not running is fear of what tomorrow does. But if you get a big number and the market tanks I think you want to buy on that weakness."
Wednesday's $500 million seven-year note issue from Philip Morris Cos Inc widened three basis points on the bid side when freed to trade, dealers said.

New issues set on Thursday included: $500 million 7.51 percent 12-year notes from GTE Corp priced at 67 basis points over the curve; $100 million 8-1/8 percent century bonds from Amgen Inc priced at 105 basis points over the long bond; and $100 million 30-year trust orginated preferred securities from PP&L Capital Trust priced as four million $25 shares with a 8.20 percent coupon.

U.S. Treasuries ended narrowly higher on Thursday as traders adjusted positions ahead of the March jobs report slated for release on Friday morning. Economists polled by Reuters forecast that non-farm payrolls grew by 196,000 jobs in March, down from 339,000 new jobs in February.
